newsitem.title: USA: Ortho-McNeil says FDA clears two drugs.
newsitem.headline: Ortho-McNeil says FDA clears two drugs.

text.p: Ortho-McNeil Pharmaceutical, a Johnson & Johnson company, said on Monday that the U.S. Food and Drug Administration cleared the antibiotic Floxin tablets as the first oral medication for the treatment of pelvic inflammatory disease.
Floxin now can be taken orally twice a day for two weeks to treat the disease.
The company said the pelvic disease, which afflicts one million women in the U.S. each year, can lead to serious complications, including infertility, the company said.
The company said Floxin has been widely used in the U.S. since 1991 to treat infections such as urinary tract infections, gonorrhea and chlamydial infection.
In a separate release, Ortho-McNeil said the FDA cleared the marketing of Levaquin to treat three bacterial respiratory infections.
The company said the drug may be used to treat community-acquired pneumonia, acute maxillary sinusitis or acute exacerbation of chronic bronchitis.
